method: Blinded idea-category labels (cycle-2 plan, phase B descriptive analysis). Packet built 2026-10-21 ~11:02 UTC, before round 4 ran: incumbent.py plus, per proposal, Hypothesis/Mechanism/Expected and the unified diff vs runs/c2-pc/incumbent.py, under opaque IDs from a seeded shuffle (seed 20261021). A fresh Claude subagent (Opus 5.5) read only the packet and defined categories by mechanism; the key was applied afterwards.

categories.name: draft-sampling
categories.definition: Changes what each initial Luna drafting call produces (number or kind of candidate files per call) while keeping the review/repair call allocation.

categories.name: call-topology
categories.definition: Rearranges how the fixed call budget is split and sequenced between Luna drafting, Sol review and Luna repair.

categories.name: judge-effort
categories.definition: Changes only the reasoning-effort setting of the Sol judge lane, with all prompts and control flow unchanged.

categories.name: reviewer-selection-procedure
categories.definition: Changes the analysis procedure Sol is told to follow when comparing candidates, picking one and finding defects, keeping the same output schema and kind of feedback.

categories.name: reviewer-feedback-enrichment
categories.definition: Changes what each Sol `fixes` entry must contain, turning a defect report into a prescriptive repair plan for Luna.

categories.name: repair-prompt-audit
categories.definition: Adds instructions to Luna's repair prompt that change how Luna carries out and checks the repair.

P1.diff_summary: Each of the three initial Luna calls gets a '## Sampling instructions' section asking for two complete Rust files (a primary and an alternative that targets its riskiest decision); a new sample_pair() extracts up to two ```rust blocks by regex (falling back to the whole text), dedups them within the call and public-tests each one, so up to six drafts enter the pool. The no-code-repair loop is changed to count calls (k - draft_calls), not entries.
P1.note: The core change matches the claim, but the diff has side effects beyond 'only initial sampling'. The review pool can now hold up to 6 candidates. The submitted set also grows: up to 6 files in the short-budget branch (k<5) and up to 7 (all drafts plus the repair) in the non-green review-repair branch, against 3 and 4 in the incumbent. Up to 6 public_test calls run instead of 3.

P2.diff_summary: Rewrites only the REVIEW prompt. Sol must run a contrastive audit before selecting: find behavioural disagreements between candidates, build distinguishing inputs, trace each candidate against the task, choose (preferring a candidate with no established defects), then audit the chosen file on the requirements that produced no disagreement. Findings must give the triggering input, required versus actual behaviour and the correction.
P2.note: Only REVIEW changes, as claimed. The diff also does a few things the hypothesis does not mention. It drops 'Audit the chosen file against the full task' and puts back a narrower step 5. It changes the selection criterion to 'prefer a candidate with no established defects'. It limits scaling findings to cases backed by the stated constraints. The contrast is also weaker than the hypothesis suggests: when greens exist, only the greens are shown, so with a single green or a single deduped candidate there is nothing to compare.

P3.diff_summary: Changes the lanes header from judge=codex/gpt-6.1-sol:medium to :high; nothing else changes.
P3.note: This is a one-line lane-config change and the diff is byte-identical to P8.

P4.diff_summary: Rewrites the REVIEW prompt so each fix is a 'repair blueprint': the requirement and the violating behaviour, a triggering input, the affected functions, the precise corrective algorithm and integration steps, and data structures, ordering, invariants and bounds. It deletes the original per-defect description lines and the ban on pseudocode, and explicitly allows language-neutral pseudocode and maths (Rust code and full solutions stay banned).
P4.note: Only the reviewer prompt changes, as claimed. The hypothesis does not mention that the diff also relaxes a reviewer constraint: the incumbent's 'Do not write ... pseudocode' prohibition is removed and pseudocode is permitted. This is the main difference from P6.

P5.diff_summary: When k>=5, replaces 3 drafts + 1 review + 1 repair with 1 draft followed by up to two rounds of (Sol review over all eligible files so far, Luna repair). Each round reuses the incumbent's greens/pool filtering, its review-keep early exit and its submission rule, and the round-2 review can pick the round-1 repair. The k<5 short-budget path is unchanged.
P5.note: The diff matches the claimed reallocation, with behavioural consequences the claim does not spell out. The round-1 'selection' is trivial because Sol sees a single candidate. A review-keep can end the run after only 2 calls. The no-code-repair branch now runs blind repairs until min(k,5) total calls: that is up to 4 repairs, and for k>5 it uses fewer calls than the incumbent's k. In the non-green branch, the final submission is the draft plus both repairs.

P6.diff_summary: Appends to the REVIEW prompt a requirement that each fix be a five-part 'repair contract' (Requirement, Witness, Cause, ordered plain-language Plan, Verify case) with one contract per root cause, and changes the JSON template to match. The incumbent's per-defect lines and its ban on Rust code, patches and pseudocode are kept.
P6.note: Only the reviewer prompt changes, as claimed. This is conceptually the same idea as P4 (Sol's findings become repair plans). Unlike P4, it keeps the pseudocode prohibition and adds an explicit Verify condition.

P7.diff_summary: Appends a COMPLETION_AUDIT block to the repair prompt, only on the review-repair branch. It tells Luna to implement the supported findings, trace triggering inputs, then walk every numbered requirement against the corrected file and fix any further established violations, before outputting one ```rust block.
P7.note: Matches the claim. The no-code-repair loop and all other calls are unchanged. The audit explicitly licenses Luna to make corrections beyond the reviewer's findings, including when the chosen candidate was public-green.

P8.diff_summary: Changes the lanes header from judge=codex/gpt-6.1-sol:medium to :high; nothing else changes.
P8.note: The diff is byte-identical to P3. Only the stated rationale and expected gain differ.

same_idea_groups.why: Both diffs are the same single-line change of the judge lane effort from medium to high; the extracted diff blocks are byte-for-byte equal (cmp/sha1 match).

Both change only the REVIEW prompt so that each fixes entry carries a prescriptive repair plan (triggering case, cause or affected logic, corrective steps, invariants and boundaries) instead of just naming the defect. The wording and structure differ. P4 replaces the per-defect lines and lifts the pseudocode ban. P6 keeps both and adds Witness/Cause/Verify labelled parts.
